q: What carbon data do EU drinks brands ask Monterrey glass container makers for?
title: Monterrey glass containers: buyer carbon data
short: Glass is not a CBAM good, but brands counting Scope 3 ask for a figure per tonne or per bottle. It covers furnace fuel, CO2 released from soda ash, limestone and dolomite, electricity, and the cullet share, which lowers both fuel and process emissions.
audience: Container glass plants in Nuevo Leon supplying beer, spirits and food brands

ul: Natural gas or fuel oil burnt in the furnace.
Process CO2 from carbonates in the batch.
Packaging and transport if the buyer asks for delivered figures.

p: Recycled glass melts at a lower temperature and carries no carbonate, so every point of cullet lowers both fuel and process CO2. State the cullet share with the figure.
Per tonne of glass for comparison, and per container using its weight, so the brand can fit it into its product footprint.

senseible: Senseible reads gas, fuel and electricity invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site and keeps lab reports and production logs beside them, so each figure can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
